newsitem.title: USA: Alabama House approves $700 mln GO highway bonds.
newsitem.headline: Alabama House approves $700 mln GO highway bonds.

text.p: Alabama's House of Representatives approved Gov. Fob James' proposal to issue $700 million of general obligation bonds for highways.
The proposal passed 95-5 Thursday and now goes to the Senate.

It would use current gasoline taxes to pay debt service on the 20-year bonds. The proposal allocates $150 million for resurfaciong roads, $150 million for bridge repairs and $81.9 million to be divided among the state's 67 counties for local projects.
The remainin $318 million would fund contruction of bypasses in urban areas and widening of several two-lane highways to four lanes.

With only nine days left in the session, James also introduced a new $80 million bond proposal to renovate the state park system. He said the debt could be paid with State Parks Fund revenues and would not require new taxes.
